question: Can a single-pass sparse causal-energy gradient select informative interventions more accurately and at lower end-to-end policy cost than iterative and conventional trained selectors?
hypothesis: From 80 witnessed familiar-context action consequences, a single source-label-only energy gradient with top-12 hard support can prioritize 16 new-context actions whose observed outcomes yield transferable causal decision accuracy superior to fully trained conventional and expensive committee alternatives at an equal 96-outcome budget.
predecessor_evidence: ENERGY-36 DEVELOPMENT_NO_GO at 966456fd95fbdafa77f2192e49ab565238134597; six-bootstrap committee 2985/3456 shifted predictions, expensive relative to random OMP.

inputs.name: Original synthetic 8-bit intervention causal source generator
inputs.source: fully source-contained SHA-256 deterministic code; no external or protected dataset

frozen_design.source_law: Signed 3-factor majority of 190 designed parity-degree1..4 and AND2 features on eight bit action patterns; deterministic per-action Bernoulli 10% witnessed corruption; hidden factors, signs, clean causal bits and held labels only evaluator-side.
frozen_design.data_budget: Each policy acquires 80 independently witnessed x0=0 actions; 16 selected x0=1 actions from a common 80-candidate pool without seeing the chosen action's consequence before selection; 96 equal total outcomes per policy, plus 16 disjoint old held and 48 disjoint new held outcomes per world. All policies, within a policy, fit on identical observed action-outcome rows; across policies actions/outcomes differ.
frozen_design.split: SHA256 context 'energy37-v1': choose old train from 128 x0=0 actions, first80 hash-ordered; next16 old held. Candidate x0=1 are counterparts of old training actions; remaining 48 x0=1 held. Deterministic order/noise evaluated from source; no held leakage.
frozen_design.algorithm: One-pass selector computes a single mean(y*x) contrastive energy gradient on observed old actions, retains top12 coordinates, no iterative optimizer/ensemble or candidate outcomes. Query uncertainty exp(-abs(phi_candidate dot w)); greedily choose top16 with +0.05 min Hamming diversity secondary criterion. OMP uncertainty and iterative energy uncertainty each fit one model; the six-bootstrap energy/OMP committees fit six models for disagreement; fixed/random have no model-fitting selection. Every policy then fully retrains all five downstream learners.
frozen_design.capacity: Same 190-feature dictionary for energy, OMP, Ridge and logistic. Both energy and OMP hard-support <=12. Energy 48 epochs, top8 gradient coordinates per epoch, step .05. OMP12 sklearn, Ridge alpha3, logistic C1 max_iter500 tol1e-8, decision tree max depth8. Committee six bootstrap replicates. No hyperparameter search using primary.
frozen_design.compute_budget: 72 worlds x 7 selectors x 5 trained downstream learners + shuffled-label negatives; single CPU, Python 3.13.5, NumPy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1. One primary run, one identical-source semantic replay, independent audit.
frozen_design.evaluator: Noiseless binary causal held prediction; threshold positive score >0 predicts +1, otherwise -1. 72x48=3456 new held predictions per arm; 72x16=1152 old held. Measure query selection plus final model fitting/inference cost (seconds) per arm; this is local component cost only, not whole system cost.

controls: Fully retrained OMP12, Ridge, logistic, decision tree for every policy
Label-shuffled sparse energy negative control for every policy
metrics: shifted held accuracy vs best other complete selection+learner combination
vs iterative energy selector with same energy learner
vs OMP uncertainty with same energy learner
positive margin against strongest alternative in >=2 of 3 source seeds
policy acquisition+fit component cost vs random+OMP12; whole process wall separately

classification_rules.supported: DEVELOPMENT_GO only if every seven frozen gate passes; still external synthetic development, not native scientific approval
classification_rules.mixed: List all gates and preserve negative or partial findings unmodified; no postscore reweighting
classification_rules.negative: DEVELOPMENT_NO_GO on any failed gate, stop candidate and preserve primary outcome without rerunning seeds for tuning
classification_rules.invalid: Cohort or source mismatch, missing strong matched controls, evaluator leakage, unequal witnessed outcome budget, source/score mismatch or failed independent audit; do not equate infrastructure failures with science.

gates.accuracy_vs_strongest: One-pass selector+energy >=3 percentage points of held shifted accuracy above highest-performing alternative among all 34 other selector+trained-learner combinations, denominator 3456.
gates.one_pass_vs_iterative: One-pass selector+energy >=1 percentage point above iterative energy uncertainty selection+energy.
gates.one_pass_vs_omp_selector: One-pass selector+energy >=1 percentage point above conventional fitted OMP12 uncertainty selection+energy.
gates.old_retention: One-pass selector+energy old held correct within <=1pp below fixed first16 selection+energy, denominator 1152.
gates.seed_stability: Strict positive shifted correct margin over strongest other complete selector+learner for at least two of three primary seeds.
gates.shuffled_negative: One-pass selector+energy shifted held correct > its shuffled-training-label energy negative by 5 percentage points.
gates.whole_policy_cost: One-pass selector acquisition + final energy fit/prediction time <= 1.5x random selector + OMP12 final fit/prediction time aggregated across the same 72 worlds.

prohibited_after_primary_run: extra data, compute or model calls unless preregistered
preregistration_note: Frozen after excluded smoke seed 99107 local PASS (3 smoke worlds and 339 independent audit assertions) and before *any* primary seed was evaluated. The source, evaluator and auditor are already committed at source_commit_sha.
